target_stack.rationale: PB-004: leadership decision, team's existing expertise

evidence.notes: runtime_ingestion active but LOW CONFIDENCE: ticketd/ops/access.log was described as a ~30-day log but actually spans a single synthetic hour (60 distinct timestamps, one date, one user, cycled twice, 2000 lines) -- see PB-brief OIQ-3. Usage-weight proportions between routes are still usable (relative mix), but perf-envelopes and any '30-day representativeness' claim are capped at low confidence. trace_capture_t1 is degraded, not fully active, for the same reason: replay T1 traces are synthesized from this log's shape, not captured real production traffic. data_census is inactive: no production DB access was granted; census queries are generated (P6) but unrun, and dirty-data policies are ASK-only.
evidence.legacy_boot_status: CONFIRMED WORKING (P7). legacy/ (ticketd/) boots for real via verification/harness/legacy_wrapper.py -- sqlite3 + Flask only (Flask installed separately, not vendored; see verification/harness/README.md). SMTP is monkeypatched at runtime (module-attribute rebind in the harness process, not a file edit) since no real smtp.internal exists in this environment. 7/7 T2 suites captured from a real running instance and validated via a legacy-vs-itself self-check (capture-legacy-goldens.sh --self-check): 0 unexpected diffs. Traces are T2 (scripted sessions), not T1 (no real production corpus was available -- see evidence.notes above), hence trace_capture_t1 stays 'degraded' not 'active' even though real code execution, not guesswork, produced every golden trace.
evidence.harness_bug_found_by_execution: OQ-010 (docs/open-questions.md): legacy leaks sqlite connections on error paths (no app.teardown_appcontext), observed to cause cascading 'database is locked' failures on the next 1-2 write requests after any request that raises mid-transaction. Found only by actually running the app under the harness, not by static reading -- recorded as a PB proposal, not silently fixed or reproduced.
